cards.text: Jeroboam, king of Israel, is in Bethel, standing beside the altar to burn incense. Suddenly a man of God from Judah shows up, sent by the word of the LORD. And friend, this man did NOT come to sit quietly in the back row.

cards.question: The man of God starts crying out by the word of the LORD, but not at the king. What does he cry out against?

cards.text: He yells, "O altar, O altar," and gives it a message from the LORD. Friend, he is preaching to the FURNITURE.

cards.question: The LORD says a son will be born to the house of David. What is his name?

cards.text: And on this very altar, that son will sacrifice the priests of the high places, and human bones will be burned on it. That altar is having the WORST day of its life.

cards.question: That same day, the man of God gives a sign from the LORD. What does the sign say will happen to the altar?

answers.text: It will sink into the ground

cards.text: King Jeroboam hears every word. He stretches out his hand toward the man of God and says, "Seize him!"

cards.question: Jeroboam's outstretched hand ___ so he can't pull it back.
True or false: the altar splits apart and the ashes pour out, just like the sign said.
Jeroboam's hand is still stuck out. What does he do?

answers.text: Asks the man of God to pray for him
Calls his own priests to pray for him
Burns more incense at the altar

cards.text: The man of God prays to the LORD, and the king's hand is restored, just like before. One minute it's seize him, next minute it's please pray for me, and friend, that is a FAST change of tune.

cards.question: Now the king wants the man of God to come home with him and refresh himself, and the king will give him a ___.
True or false: the man of God says he would go home with the king for half the king's possessions.

cards.text: He says even IF the king gave him half his possessions, he still wouldn't go, not even for bread or water in this place. Friend, I can't walk past a free cookie sample, and this man would walk past HALF A PALACE.

cards.question: The LORD commanded the man of God not to eat bread or drink water in Bethel. What was the third command?

answers.text: Don't return by the way you came
Don't speak to the king again

cards.question: True or false: the man of God leaves Bethel by a different road than the one he came on.

cards.text: Now an old prophet lives in Bethel. His sons come home and tell him everything the man of God did that day, and what he said to the king.

cards.question: The old prophet hears all about the man of God from Judah. What does he ask his sons?

cards.text: He says, "Saddle the donkey for me," and off he rides after him. This man hears ONE story and he's out the door, like me when somebody says the oven timer just went off.

cards.question: The old prophet catches up with the man of God. Where does he find him?
The old prophet invites him home to eat some bread. True or false: the man of God says yes.

cards.text: He tells the old prophet what the LORD commanded him. Then the old prophet says he's a prophet too, and an angel told him by the word of the LORD to bring the man back for bread and water.

cards.question: True or false: an angel really did tell the old prophet to bring the man of God home.
The man of God hears the old prophet's claim about the angel. What does he do?

answers.text: Goes back and eats at his house
Asks the LORD to confirm it first

cards.text: They're sitting at the table when the word of the LORD comes, and it comes to the old prophet who brought him back. I bet that's the most awkward dinner in all of Bethel.

cards.question: The LORD says the man of God defied His word, so his ___ will never reach the ___ of his fathers.

cards.text: After the meal, the old prophet saddles the donkey for him, and he heads out. On the road, a lion meets him and kills him.

cards.question: The man of God's body is left lying in the road. What is standing beside it?

cards.text: Men passing by see the body with the lion standing beside it, and they report it in the city where the old prophet lives.

cards.question: True or false: when the old prophet hears the news, he says the LORD delivered the man to the lion because he disobeyed the LORD's command.

cards.text: His sons saddle the donkey for him again, and he rides out. He finds the body in the road, with the donkey and the lion still standing beside it.

cards.question: True or false: the lion ate the body and attacked the donkey.
The old prophet lifts the body onto the donkey. What does he do with it?

answers.text: Lays it in his own tomb

cards.text: They mourn over him, crying, "Oh, my brother!" The same man who brought him back is the one weeping over him.

cards.question: The old prophet tells his sons that when he dies, they must lay his ___ beside the man of God's.
Why does the old prophet want to be buried beside the man of God?

answers.text: The man's message will surely come true
The man had asked to be buried with him
The king had commanded it for prophets

cards.text: And Jeroboam? Withered hand, split altar, and he STILL doesn't turn from his evil ways. Friend, the ALTAR cracked before the king did.

cards.question: Instead of repenting, what does Jeroboam do again?

answers.text: Makes anyone who wants it a priest
Builds a brand new altar in Dan
Sets up a third golden calf

cards.question: True or false: this sin leads to the destruction of the house of Jeroboam from the face of the earth.

cards.text: We'll let the ovens cool on that one for now. But hold on to your apron, friend, because this kingdom's story is not done yet.

findings.problem: The two blanks test exact wording the baker hasn't seen ('body' and 'tomb' in 1 Kings 13:22). Nothing earlier lets the baker reason out that the LORD's word is about his body and his fathers' tomb, so the pick is down to luck.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: The wrong words make arguable sentences. 'his body will never reach the land of his fathers' and 'his body will never reach the home of his fathers' mean nearly the same as the right answer. He dies and is buried in Bethel, away from his fathers' land in Judah, so a baker could argue for them.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: 'this sin' points back to card 12, which is no longer on screen. The question doesn't say which sin: Jeroboam appointing anyone who wanted it as a priest of the high places (1 Kings 13:33).

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: 'weeping over him' adds tears the text doesn't mention. 1 Kings 13:29-30 says he brought the body back to mourn for him and that they lamented over him.

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: The card calls Jeroboam 'king of Israel', which comes from outside the passage (1 Kings 12:20). The card cites only 1 Kings 13:1, so this outside fact has no reference.
findings.question: When a story card introduces a person with a fact from outside the passage, how should that fact's reference be given? Adding 1 Kings 12:20 to the card's single 'verses' field would break the rule that a card cites from the first verse it uses to the last. Should the outside reference go in the field anyway, go somewhere else, or be left out for well-known identifiers like this one?
